headline: Attackers exploit an unpatched Fastjson flaw for unauthenticated code execution as malvertising crews teach victims' browsers to build their own malware.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly turn a victim's own browser into a malware factory, using malicious JavaScript and the legitimate Bun runtime to assemble Windows executables in memory so no single flagged file ever crosses the wire.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SourTrade Malvertising Builds Malware Inside the Browser

emerging_trends.text: Frontier AI vendors keep sharpening the cyber offense-defense edge, as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 reaches AWS with improved coding and cybersecurity skills and a guardrail that routes the riskiest requests back to the older Opus 4.8 model.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Claude Opus 5 Lands on AWS With Sharper Cyber Skills

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews keep professionalizing their back offices, with DevMan operators running a self-service web portal that generates payloads, tracks affiliate payouts, and manages victims from one console.
emerging_trends.topic_title: DevMan Runs a Self-Service Ransomware Portal

topics.title: Claude Opus 5 Lands on AWS With Sharper Cyber Skills
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS on July 26, 2026, saying the model improves on Opus 4.8's coding and cybersecurity capabilities and hands the riskiest requests back to Opus 4.8 with a visible notice to the user.
topics.summary: Anyone with an AWS account in a supported region can call Opus 5, and API customers can configure the fallback that catches high-risk prompts. The stronger cyber capabilities cut both ways, aiding defenders and raising the ceiling for offensive misuse.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 sharpens coding and cybersecurity work on AWS

topics.title: GitHub and PyPI Add Time-Based Supply-Chain Defenses
topics.latest_developments: GitHub and the Python Package Index added a time-based mechanism to the Dependabot dependency-management tool on July 26, 2026 that delays adoption of freshly published package versions to blunt supply-chain attacks and limit their spread.
topics.summary: The cooldown gives maintainers and scanners time to catch a malicious release before Dependabot pulls it into downstream projects. Teams relying on Dependabot can enable the delay to reduce exposure to poisoned packages.

sources.title: GitHub, PyPI add time-based defenses against supply chain attacks

topics.title: SourTrade Malvertising Builds Malware Inside the Browser
topics.latest_developments: Confiant detailed on July 23, 2026 a malvertising operation it named SourTrade that ships malware in fragments and makes victims' browsers assemble the final Windows executable in memory, using the legitimate Bun runtime as its base rather than serving one complete file from a fixed URL.
topics.summary: Active since late 2024, SourTrade impersonates TradingView, Solana, and Luno to lure retail traders, running malicious JavaScript that stitches the payload together in browser memory to dodge file-based detection. Block the spoofed trading domains and watch endpoints for unexpected Bun runtime activity.

sources.title: Malvertising Sends Malware in Pieces, Then Makes the Browser Build the Executable
Malicious sites use JavaScript to build malware in browser memory

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Unpatched Fastjson RCE Flaw
topics.latest_developments: ThreatBook and Imperva reported on July 25, 2026 that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-16723, a 9.0-rated flaw in Alibaba's Fastjson 1.x JSON library for Java, before any patch exists.
topics.summary: In affected Spring Boot applications, a crafted JSON request runs code without authentication at the Java process's privilege level. Organizations running Fastjson 1.x should isolate internet-exposed services and restrict untrusted input until Alibaba ships a fix.

sources.title: Fastjson 1.x RCE Vulnerability Targeted in Attacks With No Patched Available

topics.title: DevMan Runs a Self-Service Ransomware Portal
topics.latest_developments: Swiss firm PRODAFT, tracking the operation as Funky Mantis, revealed on July 25, 2026 that the DevMan ransomware-as-a-service scheme runs a dedicated web portal that combines payload generation, finance, and victim management for its affiliates.
topics.summary: The portal lets affiliates build custom payloads, oversee earnings, and administer victims from one centralized console, lowering the skill needed to run ransomware operations. Defenders should treat DevMan as a scaling, professionally run threat rather than a lone-actor tool.

sources.title: DevMan RaaS Portal Centralizes Payload Builds, Victim Management, and Affiliate Payouts

business_politics.title: U.S.-Iran Fighting Pauses for a Second Day
business_politics.latest_developments: Neither side launched attacks for a second straight night, Iran's military said it halted retaliatory strikes on U.S. allies, and Brent crude fell back below $100 a barrel as Oman pressed a Strait of Hormuz transit deal.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Iran each held their fire while mediators worked to head off a return to full-blown war, easing two weeks of escalation that had drawn Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis into wider fighting and lifted oil above $100 a barrel.

business_politics.latest_developments: Stocks open the week facing a Federal Reserve rate decision at Chair Kevin Warsh's second meeting alongside a wave of Big Tech earnings, with an unsettled tone spreading through markets.
business_politics.summary: Investors weigh whether the Warsh-led Federal Reserve raises interest rates this week, a rare move that, paired with major technology earnings and lingering Middle East risk, could sharply move equities and bond yields.

around_town.title: Parkway East Reopens a Week Early
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT and Governor Josh Shapiro's office confirmed the new Commercial Street Bridge and the Parkway East reopen Monday evening, July 27, a full week ahead of schedule.
around_town.summary: The $95 million project slid a 22-million-pound bridge deck 102 feet into place outside the Squirrel Hill Tunnel, restoring the Parkway East (Interstate 376) after crews demolished the old Commercial Street span.

around_town.title: OpenStreetsPGH Clears Roads for People
around_town.latest_developments: Bike Pittsburgh's OpenStreetsPGH closed usually car-clogged roads through Lawrenceville and the Strip District on Sunday, July 26, opening them to walkers, cyclists, and vendors.
around_town.summary: The nonprofit Bike Pittsburgh runs the OpenStreetsPGH series, temporarily turning congested corridors into car-free public space for residents to walk, ride, and gather.

sources.title: Often car-congested Lawrenceville & Strip District roads fill with people during OpenStreetsPgh

around_teams.title: Pittman Jr. Seen Unlocking McCarthy's Passing Game
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's training-camp countdown on July 26 cast receiver Michael Pittman Jr. as the piece who can open up Mike McCarthy's passing attack alongside D.K. Metcalf and quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
around_teams.summary: As Steelers camp opens in Latrobe under new head coach Mike McCarthy, the paper argues Pittman gives Rodgers a big, reliable target across the middle to complement Metcalf on the outside.

sources.title: Steelers training camp countdown: Michael Pittman Jr. can open up Mike McCarthy's passing attack

team_usa.title: Lyles Pulls Up in 200-Meter Final
team_usa.latest_developments: Noah Lyles pulled up halfway through the 200-meter final at the U.S. track and field championships on Sunday, July 26, handing the title to USC's Garrett Kaalund in a rare loss in his signature event.
team_usa.summary: Lyles, days after winning the 100 meters at these championships, stopped mid-race in the 200 final, raising injury concerns for the reigning Olympic sprint champion.

sources.title: Lyles pulls up mid-race in 200m final at nationals
